recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing handoff with a state transformer (in-memory state schema changed).
justification: the layout of in-memory state changed, so no in-process mechanism can keep the old objects; the new process needs the old state mapped to the new schema (Kitsune/MCR-style state transfer)
a transformer skeleton was generated (old -> new, field by field, TODOs for added/retyped fields)

S6 blockers (4): github.com/gotify/server/v2/api.ApplicationParams: layout of compiled-in type ApplicationParams changed (2 functions use it); S6 replaces functions, not types; github.com/gotify/server/v2/model.Application: layout of compiled-in type Application changed (10 functions use it); S6 replaces functions, not types; github.com/gotify/server/v2/model.MessageExternal: layout of in-memory state type changed; github.com/gotify/server/v2/plugin.NewManager: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing
alternatives: rolling update if losing the in-memory state is acceptable (cold caches)
risks: no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 8 functions
type information is partial (221/221 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
state transformer must be completed and reviewed; encoding/json does not carry unexported fields, so the S5 state envelope needs an explicit DTO for them
